summary: FinanceCorp security team walked through Redwood's SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning flows and RBAC model. Customer confirmed enterprise constraints: SSO via Okta, SCIM for automated user provisioning, strict least-privilege RBAC, audit log retention requirements, and EU data residency (Frankfurt). Redwood team committed to share SAML metadata, SCIM attribute mappings, and SOC2 docs; agreed to pilot a test tenant and validate group-to-role mappings.
topics: SAML SSO configuration (IdP metadata, Assertion Consumer Service, cert rotation)
SCIM provisioning and attribute mapping (groups, custom attrs)
RBAC model (roles, least privilege, role inheritance)
Encryption and KMS basics for private deployments
SOC 2 / compliance artifacts and pen test overview
header:
Date: 2026-07-30
Start: 15:00 PT / 22:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood Solutions Engineer); Daniel Reyes (FinanceCorp CISO), Maya Singh (IT Ops Manager), Oliver Chen (Platform Engineer), Rachel Adams (Compliance), Samir Patel (Security Engineer)
Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (Redwood security pack), https://drive.google.com/financecorp-scim-list (FinanceCorp sample groups)
transcript:
00:00 Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we can give folks a couple minutes to get on. this is Lena from Redwood, im the account lead. we'll talk SSO, scim, and RBAC today.
00:15 Daniel Reyes: Hi Lena, thanks. I'm Daniel, CISO at FinanceCorp. we wanted to make sure the flow meets our compliance and ops needs. mainly okta-based SSO, scim provisioning for automated onboarding, and strict role boundaries.
00:27 Marcus Lee: Great hi Daniel, I'm Marcus on the Redwood security and infra team. I'll walk through the SAML configuration and SCIM attributes. quick note, some of our docs call the product Redwood Dedicated but the flow is the same for hosted with enterprise options.
00:42 Maya Singh: Quick Q - retention on audit logs, we have a 7 year policy for certain financial trails. is that supported?
00:51 Marcus Lee: short answer: yes we can export and ship audit logs, but retention limits depend on plan and storage add-ons. for private deployments you can push to your S3 in region for full retention. for hosted we have 3 years by default for security events, and can add long-term retention as a paid add-on.
01:10 Oliver Chen: And encryption - if we go private or VPC, can we bring our own KMS?
01:16 Priya Kapoor: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys but we also have a BYOK path for Dedicated and Private.
01:30 Daniel Reyes: Ok good. let's go into SAML specifics. our IdP is Okta. we need cert rotation procedures, SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated flows, and SCIM provisioning.
01:45 Marcus Lee: Right, for Okta we provide SAML metadata xml (we'll send it after). you configure the application in Okta, set the ACS URL to the Redwood SP endpoint, and upload our cert or we can consume your IdP metadata, either way works. we support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated.
02:00 Samir Patel: On assertion attributes, we need to map email, uid, groups, and a custom attribute for employeeType. how flexible is the attribute mapping?
02:08 Marcus Lee: Very flexible - SCIM is our recommended route for group sync but SAML assertions can carry attributes too. for SCIM we map core attributes: userName, externalId, displayName, emails, active. groups come in as group membership objects. you can add custom mapping for employeeType and we'll persist it as a user attribute.
02:28 Rachel Adams: any gotchas with SCIM group sync? we've seen collisions where users are in multiple groups and permissions stack unexpectedly.
02:37 Marcus Lee: good point. our RBAC is role-based, not group-first - you define roles in Redwood and map Okta groups to roles. if a user is in multiple groups, we resolve by evaluating the union of role bindings. for least privilege we recommend mapping narrow groups to minimal roles and avoid broad 'all-users' groups. we also support explicit deny policies for sensitive actions.
02:59 Daniel Reyes: we'd like role inheritance control so managers don't get privilege escalation by group transitivity. can you show how roles are composed?
03:10 Priya Kapoor: Sure, in the console roles are first-class objects - you can assign permissions per role, and you can compose roles. best practice we recommend: base roles with read-only, then separate admin roles that are explicitly granted. we can disable transitive inheritance or keep it explicit.
03:35 Oliver Chen: on provisioning cadence, sync every 5 minutes ok? performance wise with 20k users is that fine?
03:42 Marcus Lee: 5 minutes is supported for Dedicated/private and for hosted with high-frequency sync you may see rate limits; we can set a 1 minute throttle for SCIM on Dedicated. for 20k users we recommend dedicated capacity and batching to avoid throttles.
03:58 Maya Singh: Logging format - can we get audit logs in JSON with fields for actor, action, resource, timestamp, origin?
04:06 Marcus Lee: Yes JSON structured logs with those fields. we also include request IDs and model/runtime metadata for inference events if needed. again long term storage we ship to your S3 or GCS if you want long retention.
04:24 Daniel Reyes: certificate rotation - how do we handle key rollover without downtime?
04:30 Marcus Lee: We support key rollover windows. you can upload a new cert and set it as secondary during a transition window; Redwood will accept both old and new for a set period to avoid drop-offs. we document the recommended rotation cadence (90 days or 1 year depending on policy).
04:48 Rachel Adams: for compliance we'd like to see SOC 2 Type II and pen test results. can you share a redacted pack?
04:55 Lena Ortiz: yes we'll share the security pack. I'll send SOC2 Type II and a redacted pen test summary. note some details are under NDA but standard pack is fine.
05:10 Samir Patel: any known limitations around SCIM attributes? like nested objects?
05:16 Marcus Lee: SCIM supports groups and nested schemas but our SCIM implementation flattens custom attrs to top-level fields; if you need nested objects we can coordinate a custom mapping. we've seen this with HR systems.
05:34 Daniel Reyes: what about provisioning de-provisioning timing - immediate or delayed?
05:39 Marcus Lee: de-provisioning is immediate by default via SCIM deactivation. you can set a grace period where we disable access but keep user objects for X days. we can parameterize that per org policy.
05:55 Oliver Chen: On RBAC we want machine identities for service accounts with limited tokens. how does Redwood handle service principals?
06:03 Priya Kapoor: We support service accounts with scoped API keys and short-lived tokens. keys can be bound to roles and limited to specific model routes or endpoints. we also recommend rotating keys and using OIDC for automation.
06:21 Maya Singh: any connectors to our central secrets manager for API keys?
06:26 Marcus Lee: For private deployments you can integrate with KMS and Vault; for hosted we have integrations and vault sync options.
06:35 Daniel Reyes: Data residency - our EU business requires storage in Frankfurt (eu-central-1). Can we ensure all user data, logs, and model inputs are stored there?
06:45 Marcus Lee: Yes, we have region pinning. for EU workloads we can pin to Frankfurt for data-at-rest and logs. we do advise some telemetry (very small) for platform health that may cross regions; we can minimize or eliminate that for Private deployments.
07:02 Samir Patel: encryption in transit and at rest specifics? TLS versions, cipher suites, KMS algorithms?
07:09 Marcus Lee: We use TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 preferred) with modern cipher suites. At rest we use AES-256, and for BYOK we support RSA/ECC wrapping and HSM-backed key operations. we can provide algorithm lists in the security pack.
07:28 Rachel Adams: audit log retention and access controls - who at Redwood can see logs?
07:34 Lena Ortiz: Access is role-based. Only SRE and security engineers have elevated access, and access is logged and audited. We do per-customer isolation and require break-glass approvals for any manual access.
07:50 Daniel Reyes: ok that helps. let's dive into a demo of the SAML app config. Marcus?
07:55 Marcus Lee: Sure I'll share my screen - bear with me while i grab the config.
08:10 Marcus Lee: (screen) On the Redwood console under org settings -> SSO we generate SP metadata. here's the ACS URL: https://api.redwood.example.com/saml/acs/financecorp. you upload this into Okta and set NameID to email.
08:30 Oliver Chen: Do you support signed assertions only, or do you accept unsigned?
08:36 Marcus Lee: We require signed assertions by default. we also enforce signature validation and timestamp checks (clock skew tolerances).
08:48 Maya Singh: For SCIM mapping, can we pick which groups map to which roles?
08:52 Marcus Lee: Absolutely - mapping is via a simple table in the console: Okta group -> Redwood role. You can map multiple groups to a role or many-to-many. again careful mapping avoids privilege creep.
09:05 Daniel Reyes: show us an example for a finance-read role mapping.
09:10 Marcus Lee: here's an example: Okta group 'finance-readers' -> Redwood role 'finance_reader' with permissions: read:transactions, read:reports, no delete.
09:25 Samir Patel: can we get a dry-run mode for provisioning so we can validate mappings without impacting production users?
09:30 Marcus Lee: Yes we have a preview/dry-run for SCIM provisioning which reports what changes would be made and which role bindings would be applied. very handy for testing.
09:44 Rachel Adams: about multi-tenant concerns - if we have separate business units, can we set up sub-orgs or nested orgs?
09:51 Priya Kapoor: We support multiple child orgs under a single enterprise. Each child org can have distinct SSO config and region pins. We can explain during setup.
10:05 Daniel Reyes: governance - how do we track role changes over time? we need a changelog for audit.
10:11 Marcus Lee: All role changes and admin actions are logged with user, timestamp, and request ID. we also support webhooks to stream admin audit events to your SIEM.
10:24 Maya Singh: ok let's talk about edge cases - what happens if SCIM provisioning temporarily fails? queueing? retries?
10:31 Marcus Lee: SCIM has retries with exponential backoff and a dead-letter queue. we surface failures in the console and email admins. for Dedicated setups we can increase retry windows.
10:44 Oliver Chen: is there a way to do attribute-based access control (ABAC) combined with RBAC? e.g., allow access only if department==finance and location==EU?
10:55 Marcus Lee: We currently do RBAC + conditional rules. We support attribute conditions on role bindings (if department==finance then bind role). Full ABAC engines are on the roadmap, but conditions cover most needs.
11:12 Daniel Reyes: any known compliance gaps we should plan for?
11:17 Lena Ortiz: For hosted customers the main constraints are data residency and BYOK; if those are required we recommend Dedicated or Private. SOC 2 and ISO coverage exist; for specialized compliance (e.g., PCI with raw card storage) we'd evaluate on a case-by-case basis.
11:34 Samir Patel: What's the process for a security review/pen test from our side? can we run a penetration test against our Redwood tenant?
11:41 Marcus Lee: We allow customer-led pen tests under a coordinated schedule and NDAs; we ask you submit a test plan and we provide an approved window and contact to avoid affecting platform stability. We generally classify high-risk tests for Dedicated/private differently.
12:02 Rachel Adams: ok good. can you outline the steps to get us from PoC to production?
12:08 Lena Ortiz: Step 1: provide test tenant and IdP details. Step 2: Redwood sends SAML metadata and SCIM sample. Step 3: map groups -> roles and run dry-run. Step 4: pilot with a small user cohort. Step 5: security sign-off and production cutover. we'll send a checklist.
12:30 Daniel Reyes: sounds good. any gotchas on JIT provisioning? we prefer SCIM but sometimes need SAML JIT for partners.
12:39 Marcus Lee: SAML JIT provisioning is supported but limited; recommended approach is SCIM for full lifecycle management. for partner flows we can set up separate partner orgs or dedicated mappings.
12:55 Maya Singh: can we demo the console RBAC UI quickly?
13:00 Priya Kapoor: yep one sec. (screen) here's role editor, you can add granular permissions such as 'models.generate' 'datasets.read' 'audit.logs.view'. roles can be previewed across users.
13:25 Oliver Chen: regarding service accounts can we set a max lifetime for tokens?
13:29 Priya Kapoor: yes default is 24 hours for short-lived tokens but you can set shorter lifetimes or require rotation every 12 hours.
13:40 Samir Patel: any SAML attribute encryption support?
13:45 Marcus Lee: we support encrypted assertions if your IdP encrypts them; Redwood will decrypt with the configured key.
13:55 Daniel Reyes: let's talk about SCIM provisioning attributes map. Oliver will email the list but can you show a sample mapping?
14:02 Marcus Lee: sure: Okta 'email' -> user.email; 'firstName'->user.givenName; 'lastName'->user.familyName; Okta 'group'->roles; custom Okta 'employeeType'->user.customs.employeeType. we'll send a CSV sample.
14:24 Rachel Adams: last question - who is our escalation contact during onboarding?
14:29 Lena Ortiz: Primary is me, backup is Marcus for technical issues, and Priya is our onboarding solutions engineer. we'll include all contacts in the follow-up.
14:40 Daniel Reyes: thanks everyone. let's recap next steps.
14:44 Lena Ortiz: Recap: Marcus to send SAML/SCIM docs, Lena to send SOC2/security pack, Oliver to supply Okta group list, customer to provision test tenant and pick pilot cohort. we'll reconvene after you validate the dry-run - propose 2 weeks out.
15:00 (end)
